clue.text: A professorial sinecure, the easy one?

blocks.note: first meaning: a professorship, an endowed academic post
second meaning: a comfortable armchair, the 'easy' kind of seat

explanation.surface: A cynic sneers that a university professorship is a soft job, the easiest post going.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second half as a play on words: an easy chair is a piece of furniture, not an undemanding job.
explanation.definitionFit: A university professorship is called a chair, and a comfortable upholstered armchair is an easy chair.

clue.text: Simeon as newspaper-man?

blocks.note: surface reading: an early Christian figure somehow working on a newspaper
setter's reading: Simeon Stylites lived for decades on top of a pillar, so he was a pillar man

explanation.walkthrough: Saint Simeon Stylites spent 37 years living on top of a stone pillar in Syria; a pillar is a column, and a regular newspaper writer has a column.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who writes a regular signed feature in a paper is named after that feature, the column.

clue.text: “To what green — was Keats's heifer being led?-

definitions.text: To what green — was Keats's heifer being led?

blocks.clueFragment: To what green — was Keats's heifer being led?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about a cow being taken to a village green or pasture
setter's reading: Ode on a Grecian Urn asks 'To what green ___, O mysterious priest, / Lead'st thou that heifer'; the blank is the missing word

explanation.walkthrough: This is a quotation to complete: in Keats's ode a priest leads a garlanded heifer to sacrifice, so the green thing she goes to is where offerings are made.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the heifer is a sacrificial victim, and sacrifices are offered on a raised table in a temple.

clue.text: Particular esteem

blocks.note: first meaning: a detail or point, as in 'correct in every particular'
second meaning: admiration or high regard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' reads as an adjective describing the esteem, but it is a noun here, a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In every respect' means in every detail or point, and to hold someone in respect is to regard them highly.

clue.text: Scarlet emblem of English admiral and French marshal in his time

blocks.clueFragment: Scarlet emblem of English admiral and French marshal in his time
blocks.note: surface reading: a red badge belonging to two military men of the Napoleonic era
setter's reading: Admiral Blake plus Marshal Ney make Blakeney, Sir Percy Blakeney of Baroness Orczy's novels

explanation.surface: Two commanders on opposing sides of the Napoleonic wars share a red badge.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Percy Blakeney is the Scarlet Pimpernel, the English hero who rescues aristocrats in revolutionary France and signs his notes with a little red flower; Blake was a 17th-century English admiral and Ney one of Napoleon's marshals.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small red wild flower, the sign the fictional hero Blakeney left behind.

clue.text: Charge small sum on Latin translation

indicators.note: a translation renders words in a different form, so the letters of the Latin word are recast

blocks.note: P, a penny, is a small sum of money
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A bill charges a small fee for translating a Latin text.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a plaint is the written statement of an accusation or complaint brought before a court.

clue.text: Fish rising in lake, including one of poor quality

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards, back to front
something including another holds it inside itself
one thing sitting in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a mere is a lake or pond
a common sea fish
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fish surfaces in a lake that also holds a rather poor specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish turned upwards takes the one after its first letter, and that whole group sits in the middle of the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre is only ordinary or second-rate, never better than middling standard.

clue.text: Marine creature which is a feature in eastern United States

indicators.note: the feature is placed inside the outer letters taken from the rest of the phrase

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
the chin is a feature of the face
abbreviation for United States

explanation.surface: A sea animal turns out to be a landmark of the eastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The word also names a moulding on a classical column capital, which the surface's 'feature' faintly hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinus is the zoological name for the common sea urchin, a spiny animal of the seabed.

clue.text: Rest troubled by the dark waters of the moon?

blocks.note: night is the dark time of day
a mare is a dark plain on the moon, named by early astronomers as a sea

explanation.surface: Someone's sleep is disturbed by gazing at the shadowy seas of the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The lunar 'seas', such as the Sea of Tranquillity, are each called a mare, Latin for sea; there is no water in them, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightening dream spoils a night's sleep, so it is sleep that has been disturbed.

clue.text: A story about for instance a feudal lord

indicators.note: about means around, so the story wraps round what follows

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: A tale is told about some medieval nobleman, offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Under feudalism a liege was the superior to whom vassals owed allegiance and service.

clue.text: Home of idleness not as dull, as it might be

indicators.note: the letters are shown as they might be, that is in some other possible order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A haven of laziness is not as boring as one might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey the lotus-eaters lived in drowsy contentment, forgetting all ambition, which makes the definition fit neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of the lotus-eaters is a place of dreamy indolence, so it is a home of idleness.

clue.text: In Holland it is silver in colour

definitions.note: describes the place rather than naming it

indicators.note: the precious metal goes inside the word for a colour

blocks.note: a hue is a colour
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Something in the Netherlands is said to be silvery in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description, 'it is in Holland', so the answer is a Dutch place; the city's name is usually given with 'The'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of the Dutch government is a city in Holland, the western province of the Netherlands.

clue.text: The widow Capet, victim of 22 ac

definitions.text: The widow Capet, victim of 22 ac

blocks.note: surface reading: a bereaved woman called Capet; setter's reading: the name the French revolutionaries gave Louis XVI's widow
setter's reading: the fairest-award contest of 22 across is read instead as the verdict of a court in Paris

explanation.walkthrough: After Louis XVI, 'Citizen Capet', was guillotined, his queen was tried as the widow Capet by the Revolutionary Tribunal in Paris and executed in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian-born queen of France was condemned by a Paris court, a punning victim of a Parisian judgement.

clue.text: Tavern crony we hear is in an institution

definitions.note: describes the person rather than naming them

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the phrase is matched by its sound

blocks.note: a tavern is an inn and a crony is a mate, a pal

explanation.surface: A pub drinking companion, so rumour has it, has been locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner or patient confined in a jail, asylum or hospital is one who lives in such a place.

clue.text: Sensational performance by new model Hindu hero

indicators.note: a new version of the word is a fresh arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Rama is the hero of the Hindu epic the Ramayana

explanation.surface: A sensational stage show stars a newly fashioned figure of an Indian hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a play with exaggerated characters and thrilling, sensational plot twists.

clue.text: One kind of band and a way to make another (army style?)

blocks.note: a brass band is one kind of band
taken as written
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Setting out ways of forming bands, one of them in a military style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another kind of band, and 'army style' hints that it is worn on the arm, as by soldiers or officials.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassard is a badge-bearing armband, a strip of cloth worn round the upper arm.

clue.text: Levantine capitalist to go in for ornamental metal-work

definitions.text: to go in for ornamental metal-work

blocks.note: first meaning: a native of Damascus, the capital of Syria in the Levant

blocks.clueFragment: to go in for ornamental metal-work
blocks.note: second meaning: as a verb, to decorate metal with inlaid wavy patterns of gold or silver

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitalist' reads as a financier but means simply someone from a capital city; the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Damascus is a Damascene, and the craft of inlaying steel, named after that city's blades, is to damascene.

clue.text: Support isn't common in a cockfight?

indicators.note: the slang contraction is placed in the word for the bout

blocks.note: a main is an old word for a cockfighting match
ain't is the common, nonstandard form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether backing is unusual at a cockfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' means vulgar or nonstandard speech here, not ordinary or shared; a main was a series of matches between fighting cocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain is to support, either by keeping something going or by providing for someone financially.

clue.text: Met with large entanglement of wire

indicators.note: things in an entanglement are knotted and twisted out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ran into a big tangle of wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wire' looks like the material of the tangle, but it is the definition: in older usage, to wire someone was to send a cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram was sent over telegraph wires, so 'a wire' became a colloquial name for one.

clue.text: Spinning-wheel devotee

blocks.note: surface reading: an enthusiast for the old craft of spinning yarn
setter's reading: the wheel that spins in a casino, roulette

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen makes it look like the cottage spinning wheel; read it as a wheel that spins, and the devotee is at the roulette table.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on roulette bets money on chance, which is what a punter at games of luck does.

clue.text: It sounds frightfully comical

blocks.note: surface reading: something seems extremely funny, frightfully meaning very
setter's reading: a cry of fright is a sound, and the same word names something hilarious

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightfully' is the old upper-class intensifier, very; taken literally it points to a shriek of terror.
explanation.definitionFit: A piercing cry of terror shares its name with a person or thing so funny it is called 'a real' one.

clue.text: Original material for newspaper, it's otherwise for the scrivener

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the short word is set out in a different order

blocks.note: copy is the text a journalist submits to be printed
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Copy written for a newspaper is something quite different for an old clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: Copy for a paper is the original text, but for a scrivener copying is the whole job, which gives the surface its twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrivener was a professional writer who copied out documents by hand before printing and typewriters.

clue.text: Winnie raised old English bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, a raised word is lifted so it reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: Winnie-the-Pooh, A. A. Milne's bear
OE is the abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: Winnie, perhaps a pet's name, brought up an old English bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested pinkish bird with barred black and white wings, named after its call.

clue.text: The fairest award for classical students

definitions.text: The fairest award for classical students

blocks.clueFragment: The fairest award for classical students
blocks.note: surface reading: the most even-handed prize given to pupils of Latin and Greek
setter's reading: the award made to the fairest, the golden apple inscribed 'to the fairest' in Greek myth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairest' reads as most just, but means most beautiful: the Trojan prince chose Aphrodite over Hera and Athena, and students of the classics know the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prince's choice of which goddess was most beautiful is the famous mythological verdict sparking the Trojan War.

clue.text: Miller, J — some card

blocks.note: first meaning: Joe Miller, the comic actor whose name was put on a famous book of jests
second meaning: a wild card in a pack, and also a comical person, since a card is a wag

explanation.walkthrough: Joe Miller's Jests appeared in 1739, and 'a Joe Miller' came to mean a stale gag; the initial J. stands for Joe, written like a name in a register.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller of gags is a wag, and the extra wild card in a pack carries the jester's image.

clue.text: Flowing like mead, say, at the Magna Carta scene

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be taken by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: Runnymede, the meadow by the Thames where King John sealed Magna Carta in 1215
the drink mead sounds like the end of the place name

explanation.surface: Honey wine is poured at the meadow where the barons met King John.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is what comes before the sound of 'mead' in the place name, so the clue's 'like mead' means 'alongside mead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something runny is liquid enough to flow freely, like honey or a soft-boiled egg yolk.

clue.text: Bird returns to circle a native village

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
to circle something is to go right round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: the lark is a songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird comes back to wheel over a village.
explanation.definitionFit: In southern Africa a kraal is a traditional village of huts, often enclosed by a fence.

clue.text: Fruit I can get cooked in this device

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered, so these letters are prepared in a new order
the mixed letters go in the fruit, inside it

blocks.note: an apple is a fruit
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they can cook fruit in this kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This device' points at the cooker the surface implies; the scrambled letters sit before the fruit's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a machine or device for a household task, such as a cooker or mixer.

clue.text: Anagrammatize “back row

blocks.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains or houses

explanation.surface: An instruction to jumble the letters of the words 'back row'.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like an anagram of 'back row', which gives nothing; the first word is the definition, and the quoted words build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an anagram of a word is to put its letters into a different order.

clue.text: Herb's no waiter, it's said

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the word is matched by sound

blocks.note: the proverb says time and tide wait for no man, so time never waits for anyone

explanation.surface: A man called Herb is not a waiter, someone reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' reads as a man's name, the abbreviation of Herbert; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a small aromatic plant whose leaves are used to flavour cooking.
